.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-skill-task-list.md:5897:/home/jbb/.codex/sessions/2026/07/07/rollout-2026-07-07T18-53-38-019f3c6d-38a5-7e23-a238-904176322f0c.jsonl:7:{"timestamp":"2026-07-07T11:53:41.990Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"user_message","message":"$human-context-synthesis\n\nYou are processing one decision-os card from the active workspace.\n\nTreat the following source card as the complete incoming card content for this run.\n\nSource card id: card-0b144d6a-16a1-4cc2-9b9f-32aabafd5b4a\nSource card title: Decision OS Context\n\nSource card content:\n```markdown\n::html[Context report summary](.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/assets/context-report-summary/context-report-summary.html)\n\n---\n\n## A. Product Context\n\n1. **Current product state.** `decision-os` is a local browser canvas, a TypeScript backend ledger server, and workspace-local `.decision-os` data. The active repo workspace is dogfooding the product through `.decision-os/state.json`, which currently exposes `specs`, `data`, `performances`, and `tasks-system`.\n2. **Surface area.** The current surface includes route-addressed ledger tabs, a ledgers overview canvas, cards, zones, groups, relationships, canvas pan/zoom, selection, clipboard copy/paste, card resize, card Markdown, card fields, image carousels, HTML card assets, right-side threads, voice notes, transcription retry, live refresh, the `ledger-cli`, and the `generator-cli`.\n3. **Active workflows.** Operators inspect and edit ledgers on the canvas, create or move cards/zones/groups, review specs and performance evidence, paste images/files into threads, record voice notes, ask agents to treat unanswered notes, maintain card and zone summaries, and use report/mockup cards for PO analysis work.\n4. **Actors and roles.** The **operator** owns decisions, notes, approvals, and workspace intent. The **agent** reads threads, changes repo or ledger state, and replies in `# AGENT` sections. The **watcher** concept monitors unanswered notes. The **backend server** owns filesystem hydration and mutation. The **frontend runtime** owns transient interaction state. The **ledger CLI** is the maintenance and agent queue surface. The **OpenAI transcription provider** is optional and configured per workspace.\n5. **Adoption state.** Adoption evidence is internal and active: the repo workspace contains `289` spec cards, `40` data-model cards, `9` performance cards, and `27` task-system cards. No external customer analytics, production usage metrics, or support evidence were found in this research pass.\n6. **Active specs.** `specs.json` covers boot, navigation, canvas rendering, zones, selection, cards, threads, voice, refresh, groups, relationships, media, CLI tooling, generator tooling, and implementation architecture. `tasks-system.json` is the current Next Features surface and contains work around watcher loops, summary maintenance, task queues, report UX, and goal-object UX.\n7. **Known friction.** Threads currently carry too many responsibilities: conversation history, work queue, lock, status model, progress log, and recovery surface. Performance notes show drag and pan risk around browser frame production, layout-position writes, zone label reads, overlay rerenders, rich card surfaces, and relationship routing. Report UX notes show unresolved product boundaries for whether reports should be a card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, or embedded reader.\n\n---\n\n## B. Technical Context\n\n1. **Platform.** The backend is a Node/TypeScript HTTP server run through `tsx`; the frontend is a frameworkless TypeScript browser runtime served without a bundler; tests use Node's native test runner and Playwright-style browser specs; card syntax highlighting uses `highlight.js`.\n2. **Architecture.** The repo is split into `backend`, `frontend`, `ledger-cli`, `generator-cli`, `shared`, `tests`, `operations`, and workspace `.decision-os` files. The launcher `bin/decision-os-server.mjs` derives `DECISION_OS_FRONTEND_ROOT` and `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH`, then starts `backend/src/server.ts` from the target workspace cwd.\n3. **Services and APIs.** The backend serves app routes `/`, `/ledgers`, and `/<ledgerId>`, state and ledger APIs under `/decision-os/state`, `/decision-os/<tab>`, `/decision-os/ledgers`, and `/decision-os/ledgers-canvas`, live refresh at `/api/ledger-content-events`, uploads at `/api/thread-image-upload`, `/api/thread-file-upload`, and `/api/voice-upload`, and transcription at `/api/transcribe` plus `/api/transcribe/retry`.\n4. **Data model.** `.decision-os/state.json` owns the ledger registry. Each ledger JSON owns `cards`, `annotations`, `relationships`, `viewport`, `threadFiles`, and related structured fields. Card bodies are durable Markdown files referenced by `comment.contentFile`. Thread histories are durable Markdown files under `.decision-os/threads/...`. Image layout persists through `imageSizes` in card JSON.\n5. **State ownership.** The filesystem is the canonical state store. The backend hydrates card Markdown and thread files into ledger responses, strips hydrated notes before writing, validates mutations, writes ledger JSON, writes card content files, and writes thread content files. The frontend owns transient state such as `activeTab`, `viewport`, `selection`, active tool, card tab state, open thread, draft text, scroll position, clipboard, and voice capture state.\n6. **Integrations.** Workspace settings in `.decision-os/.settings.json` can configure transcription with `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `openaiApiKey` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`. The server also integrates with local filesystem watchers, local static asset serving, browser media capture, and the local CLI tools.\n7. **Permissions and security.** The default server host is `127.0.0.1`. Workspace asset serving is constrained to the active `.decision-os` root and allowed image, thread-file, or active-card asset paths. API keys and uploaded voice files are intended to stay local and uncommitted.\n8. **Observability.** The frontend and generator surfaces emit local telemetry facts. Performance evidence is stored in `operations/canvas-performance-study-2026-05-29.md` and `.decision-os/cards/performances/...`. Verification surfaces include `npm run typecheck:frontend`, `npm run typecheck:backend`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:front-back`, and live verification scripts under `tools/live-verify`.\n9. **Deployment.** Current deployment is local workspace execution, not hosted SaaS. Operator-facing sessions should run the detached launcher from the target workspace cwd, redirect logs under `/tmp`, and verify the HTTP route before reporting a URL.\n\n---\n\n## C. UX Context\n\n1. **Journeys.** A user opens a ledger route, reviews the canvas, selects or creates cards/zones/groups, edits geometry or content, opens the thread panel with `A`, writes or records notes, receives agent replies, reviews card media or report mockups, and can use CLI workflows for maintenance or agent treatment.\n2. **Screens and regions.** The main UX includes the tab registry, full-canvas ledger surface, toolbox, canvas controls, card detail layer, card overview layer, card description and fields tabs, relationship overlays, zone/group labels, deletion confirmation modals, right-side thread inspector, terminal-style composer, voice dock, telemetry/status copy, and the hidden ledgers overview.\n3. **States.** Important UI states include route mode, active ledger, viewport, zoom/detail mode, active tool, selection, grouped selection, clipboard, open card tab, low-detail versus hydrated card rendering, thread open/closed, draft restored, scroll restored, optimistic note pending, voice recording, transcription uploading, transcription failed, retry available, modal open, and external refresh received.\n4. **Entry points.** Primary entry points are `/`, `/ledgers`, `/<ledgerId>`, the tab registry, card/zone/group controls, the toolbox, keyboard shortcuts, thread buttons, thread upload/paste controls, voice controls, `ledger-cli`, and server launch commands.\n5. **Handoffs.** Operator notes hand off to agents through thread files. Agent replies hand back through `# AGENT` notes and durable card edits. Voice capture hands off from browser media capture to upload, transcription, optimistic note update, and retry. External filesystem edits hand off to the client through server-sent refresh events. Card Markdown hands off to backend hydration and frontend Markdown/media rendering.\n6. **Information architecture.** The current workspace separates **Specs** for behavior contracts, **Data** for base classes and relationships, **Performances** for measured canvas performance evidence, and **Tasks System** for Next Features. At the object level, cards, zones, groups, relationships, and threads are the main navigable units.\n7. **Accessibility.** The implemented keyboard contract includes `A`, `X`, `Esc`, `Del`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+V`, and `Ctrl+D`. Deletion confirmations support keyboard handling. Some rendered controls expose labels or titles. Full WCAG coverage, screen-reader behavior, focus order, and color-contrast audits were not verified in this pass.\n8. **Copy and language.** Agent replies must be English. Thread copy uses `# OPERATOR` and `# AGENT` sections. Durable card content should stay concrete, implementation-ready, and traceable to source files or ledgers. The in-app Keys panel should remain the operator-facing keyboard contract.\n9. **Interaction constraints.** Expensive card detail is hydrated only when detail is visible. Pan/zoom and drag must preserve responsive frame production. Delete actions require confirmation. Thread and voice tooling must not steal editing keystrokes. Media dimensions must persist independent of canvas zoom. HTML embeds must stay under allowed card asset paths.\n\n---\n\n## D. Context Boundaries\n\n1. **In scope.** This context covers the current `decision-os` repo, the active repo-local `.decision-os` workspace, existing code, existing docs, active ledgers, task cards, performance notes, thread model, CLI model, and local runtime behavior visible from source inspection.\n2. **Out of scope.** This context does not cover a hosted deployment, multi-tenant permissions, billing, external customer research, market positioning, production analytics, support tickets, or non-repo workspaces.\n3. **Unverified areas.** This pass did not start a browser session, run automated tests, inspect live decision-os workspace state, validate a real transcription API key, measure current browser performance, audit accessibility with assistive technology, or confirm external operator adoption beyond repo evidence.\n4. **Source gaps.** There is no discovered analytics baseline, customer interview set, support ticket sample, hosted deployment runbook, centralized telemetry sink, or current CI result attached to this note. Some README examples still describe older `tabs` wording while current state uses a `ledgers` registry.\n5. **Cross-team dependencies.** The only confirmed dependency outside the local repo is optional OpenAI transcription configuration. Product-boundary decisions for reports, work queues, watcher agents, and goal objects remain operator-owned unless a future card assigns explicit ownership.\n6. **Evidence sources.** Primary evidence came from `README.md`, `.decision-os/state.json`, `.decision-os/specs.json`, `.decision-os/data.json`, `.decision-os/performances.json`, `.decision-os/tasks-system.json`, `backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts`, `backend/src/business/ledger/helper/apply-ledger-mutation.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/boot/controller/boot-surface.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/render-ledger-surface.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/input/controller/handle-keyboard.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/thread/effect/render-thread-panel.ts`, `.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-agent-autonomy-work-queue.md`, `.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-2395850a-c528-4689-a138-73a30b684602.md`, and `.decision-os/cards/performances/...`.\n\n```\n\nWrite the final result to this Markdown file: /home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-codex-skill-1783425215516-e1916f75.md\n\nUse English only.\nDo not edit the source card.\nDo not edit ledger JSON manually.\nKeep unrelated files unchanged.\nWhen finished, ensure the Markdown file contains the useful result for the operator.","images":[],"local_images":[],"text_elements":[]}}

Product Context\n     6\t\n     7\t1. **Current product state.** `decision-os` is a local browser canvas, a TypeScript backend ledger server, and workspace-local `.decision-os` data. The active repo workspace is dogfooding the product through `.decision-os/state.json`, which currently exposes `specs`, `data`, `performances`, and `tasks-system`.\n     8\t2. **Surface area.** The current surface includes route-addressed ledger tabs, a ledgers overview canvas, cards, zones, groups, relationships, canvas pan/zoom, selection, clipboard copy/paste, card resize, card Markdown, card fields, image carousels, HTML card assets, right-side threads, voice notes, transcription retry, live refresh, the `ledger-cli`, and the `generator-cli`.\n     9\t3. **Active workflows.** Operators inspect and edit ledgers on the canvas, create or move cards/zones/groups, review specs and performance evidence, paste images/files into threads, record voice notes, ask agents to treat unanswered notes, maintain card and zone summaries, and use report/mockup cards for PO analysis work.\n    10\t4. **Actors and roles.** The **operator** owns decisions, notes, approvals, and workspace intent. The **agent** reads threads, changes repo or ledger state, and replies in `# AGENT` sections. The **watcher** concept monitors unanswered notes. The **backend server** owns filesystem hydration and mutation. The **frontend runtime** owns transient interaction state. The **ledger CLI** is the maintenance and agent queue surface. The **OpenAI transcription provider** is optional and configured per workspace.\n    11\t5. **Adoption state.** Adoption evidence is internal and active: the repo workspace contains `289` spec cards, `40` data-model cards, `9` performance cards, and `27` task-system cards. No external customer analytics, production usage metrics, or support evidence were found in this research pass.\n    12\t6. **Active specs.** `specs.json` covers boot, navigation, canvas rendering, zones, selection, cards, threads, voice, refresh, groups, relationships, media, CLI tooling, generator tooling, and implementation architecture. `tasks-system.json` is the current Next Features surface and contains work around watcher loops, summary maintenance, task queues, report UX, and goal-object UX.\n    13\t7. **Known friction.** Threads currently carry too many responsibilities: conversation history, work queue, lock, status model, progress log, and recovery surface. Performance notes show drag and pan risk around browser frame production, layout-position writes, zone label reads, overlay rerenders, rich card surfaces, and relationship routing. Report UX notes show unresolved product boundaries for whether reports should be a card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, or embedded reader.\n    14\t\n    15\t---\n    16\t\n    17\t## B. Technical Context\n    18\t\n    19\t1. **Platform.** The backend is a Node/TypeScript HTTP server run through `tsx`; the frontend is a frameworkless TypeScript browser runtime served without a bundler; tests use Node's native test runner and Playwright-style browser specs; card syntax highlighting uses `highlight.js`.\n    20\t2. **Architecture.** The repo is split into `backend`, `frontend`, `ledger-cli`, `generator-cli`, `shared`, `tests`, `operations`, and workspace `.decision-os` files. The launcher `bin/decision-os-server.mjs` derives `DECISION_OS_FRONTEND_ROOT` and `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH`, then starts `backend/src/server.ts` from the target workspace cwd.\n    21\t3. **Services and APIs.** The backend serves app routes `/`, `/ledgers`, and `/<ledgerId>`, state and ledger APIs under `/decision-os/state`, `/decision-os/<tab>`, `/decision-os/ledgers`, and `/decision-os/ledgers-canvas`, live refresh at `/api/ledger-content-events`, uploads at `/api/thread-image-upload`, `/api/thread-file-upload`, and `/api/voice-upload`, and transcription at `/api/transcribe` plus `/api/transcribe/retry`.\n    22\t4. **Data model.** `.decision-os/state.json` owns the ledger registry. Each ledger JSON owns `cards`, `annotations`, `relationships`, `viewport`, `threadFiles`, and related structured fields. Card bodies are durable Markdown files referenced by `comment.contentFile`. Thread histories are durable Markdown files under `.decision-os/threads/...`. Image layout persists through `imageSizes` in card JSON.\n    23\t5. **State ownership.** The filesystem is the canonical state store. The backend hydrates card Markdown and thread files into ledger responses, strips hydrated notes before writing, validates mutations, writes ledger JSON, writes card content files, and writes thread content files. The frontend owns transient state such as `activeTab`, `viewport`, `selection`, active tool, card tab state, open thread, draft text, scroll position, clipboard, and voice capture state.\n    24\t6. **Integrations.** Workspace settings in `.decision-os/.settings.json` can configure transcription with `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `openaiApiKey` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`. The server also integrates with local filesystem watchers, local static asset serving, browser media capture, and the local CLI tools.\n    25\t7. **Permissions and security.** The default server host is `127.0.0.1`. Workspace asset serving is constrained to the active `.decision-os` root and allowed image, thread-file, or active-card asset paths. API keys and uploaded voice files are intended to stay local and uncommitted.\n    26\t8. **Observability.** The frontend and generator surfaces emit local telemetry facts. Performance evidence is stored in `operations/canvas-performance-study-2026-05-29.md` and `.decision-os/cards/performances/...`. Verification surfaces include `npm run typecheck:frontend`, `npm run typecheck:backend`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:front-back`, and live verification scripts under `tools/live-verify`.\n    27\t9. **Deployment.** Current deployment is local workspace execution, not hosted SaaS. Operator-facing sessions should run the detached launcher from the target workspace cwd, redirect logs under `/tmp`, and verify the HTTP route before reporting a URL.\n    28\t\n    29\t---\n    30\t\n    31\t## C. UX Context\n    32\t\n    33\t1. **Journeys.** A user opens a ledger route, reviews the canvas, selects or creates cards/zones/groups, edits geometry or content, opens the thread panel with `A`, writes or records notes, receives agent replies, reviews card media or report mockups, and can use CLI workflows for maintenance or agent treatment.\n    34\t2. **Screens and regions.** The main UX includes the tab registry, full-canvas ledger surface, toolbox, canvas controls, card detail layer, card overview layer, card description and fields tabs, relationship overlays, zone/group labels, deletion confirmation modals, right-side thread inspector, terminal-style composer, voice dock, telemetry/status copy, and the hidden ledgers overview.\n    35\t3. **States.** Important UI states include route mode, active ledger, viewport, zoom/detail mode, active tool, selection, grouped selection, clipboard, open card tab, low-detail versus hydrated card rendering, thread open/closed, draft restored, scroll restored, optimistic note pending, voice recording, transcription uploading, transcription failed, retry available, modal open, and external refresh received.\n    36\t4. **Entry points.** Primary entry points are `/`, `/ledgers`, `/<ledgerId>`, the tab registry, card/zone/group controls, the toolbox, keyboard shortcuts, thread buttons, thread upload/paste controls, voice controls, `ledger-cli`, and server launch commands.\n    37\t5. **Handoffs.** Operator notes hand off to agents through thread files. Agent replies hand back through `# AGENT` notes and durable card edits. Voice capture hands off from browser media capture to upload, transcription, optimistic note update, and retry. External filesystem edits hand off to the client through server-sent refresh events. Card Markdown hands off to backend hydration and frontend Markdown/media rendering.\n    38\t6. **Information architecture.** The current workspace separates **Specs** for behavior contracts, **Data** for base classes and relationships, **Performances** for measured canvas performance evidence, and **Tasks System** for Next Features. At the object level, cards, zones, groups, relationships, and threads are the main navigable units.\n    39\t7. **Accessibility.** The implemented keyboard contract includes `A`, `X`, `Esc`, `Del`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+V`, and `Ctrl+D`. Deletion confirmations support keyboard handling. Some rendered controls expose labels or titles. Full WCAG coverage, screen-reader behavior, focus order, and color-contrast audits were not verified in this pass.\n    40\t8. **Copy and language.** Agent replies must be English. Thread copy uses `# OPERATOR` and `# AGENT` sections. Durable card content should stay concrete, implementation-ready, and traceable to source files or ledgers. The in-app Keys panel should remain the operator-facing keyboard contract.\n    41\t9. **Interaction constraints.** Expensive card detail is hydrated only when detail is visible. Pan/zoom and drag must preserve responsive frame production. Delete actions require confirmation. Thread and voice tooling must not steal editing keystrokes. Media dimensions must persist independent of canvas zoom. HTML embeds must stay under allowed card asset paths.\n    42\t\n    43\t---\n    44\t\n    45\t## D. Context Boundaries\n    46\t\n    47\t1. **In scope.** This context covers the current `decision-os` repo, the active repo-local `.decision-os` workspace, existing code, existing docs, active ledgers, task cards, performance notes, thread model, CLI model, and local runtime behavior visible from source inspection.\n    48\t2. **Out of scope.** This context does not cover a hosted deployment, multi-tenant permissions, billing, external customer research, market positioning, production analytics, support tickets, or non-repo workspaces.\n    49\t3. **Unverified areas.** This pass did not start a browser session, run automated tests, inspect live decision-os workspace state, validate a real transcription API key, measure current browser performance, audit accessibility with assistive technology, or confirm external operator adoption beyond repo evidence.\n    50\t4. **Source gaps.** There is no discovered analytics baseline, customer interview set, support ticket sample, hosted deployment runbook, centralized telemetry sink, or current CI result attached to this note. Some README examples still describe older `tabs` wording while current state uses a `ledgers` registry.\n    51\t5. **Cross-team dependencies.** The only confirmed dependency outside the local repo is optional OpenAI transcription configuration. Product-boundary decisions for reports, work queues, watcher agents, and goal objects remain operator-owned unless a future card assigns explicit ownership.\n    52\t6. **Evidence sources.** Primary evidence came from `README.md`, `.decision-os/state.json`, `.decision-os/specs.json`, `.decision-os/data.json`, `.decision-os/performances.json`, `.decision-os/tasks-system.json`, `backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts`, `backend/src/business/ledger/helper/apply-ledger-mutation.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/boot/controller/boot-surface.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/render-ledger-surface.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/input/controller/handle-keyboard.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/thread/effect/render-thread-panel.ts`, `.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-agent-autonomy-work-queue.md`, `.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-2395850a-c528-4689-a138-73a30b684602.md`, and `.decision-os/cards/performances/...`.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f3d81-f556-7433-9b32-66a812c294b5"}}}
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-skill-task-list.md:5928:/home/jbb/.codex/sessions/2026/07/09/rollout-2026-07-09T12-44-43-019f4568-2f76-7bb0-93c2-fbbbed5c62b6.jsonl:86:{"timestamp":"2026-07-09T05:46:44.863Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_GIXrjkLCEv7YjfBBzR0z286e","output":"Chunk ID: 778d62\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1892\nOutput:\n---\nname: executor-spec\ndescription: Transform Specs, Data Model, Runtime State and executor-stack analysis output into a master ledger then used to create the scaffold of the whole codebase or codebase section. Read the WHOLE document, not only a subsection. CREATE the master-ledger document FIRST, then WRITE each section one AFTER the other.\n---\n\n# Executor Spec\n\n## A. Formatting Contract\n\n1. **Headings:** use `H2` card sections with uppercase letters: `## A. Scope`, `## B. Contract`, `## C. Acceptance Criteria`.\n2. **Dividers:** put `---` between card sections.\n3. **Lists:** write section content as numbered list items: `1.`, `2.`, `3.`.\n4. **Bold:** use **bold** for the important words that carry the point.\n5. **Backticks:** use `backticks` for technical, secondary, exact, or literal terms: file paths, routes, config keys, commands, IDs, statuses, branch names, code symbols, and literal values.\n\nThe purpose is to turn `stack analysis` into a `Master Ledger`, containing the complete or partial scaffold, depending on the `operator` demand. \n\n---\n\n## A. Nomenclature and Definitions\n\n### A.1 Spec\n\n- A `spec` is an `operator`-authored truth constraint over the system: it defines an expected property, behavior, capability, or invariant that must hold in *all applicable situations*, **independent of how the system is implemented**.\n\n- An `Anti-Spec` is an operator-authored truth constraint that says what the system must not do, must reject, or must never infer.\n\n### A.2 Data Model\n\nA `Data Model` is the `operator`-authored schema of the system’s *durable and contractual data*: the entities, tables, records, fields, identities, relationships, and constraints that the implementation must *store, load, validate, and exchange*.\n\n### A.3 Runtime State\n`Runtime State` is the current *in-memory state* of the running system: the session, UI, interaction, process, cache, selection, pending operation, telemetry, and *transient values* that can change *while the system executes* and that may be derived from, synchronized with, or eventually persisted into the `Data Model`.\n\n### A.4 Root Block\n\n- A Root Block is a top-level system part with its own runtime or ownership boundary.  \n\n- It can be a frontend, backend, mobile app, CLI, worker, engine, library, QA harness, or shared contract package when it owns its own project shape.  \n\n- Root blocks should have already been defined by the previous `executor-stack` step.\n\n- A root block is a package/app/engine/tool with its own source, package, build process, metadata, README/AGENTS guidance, runtime entrypoint, data, generated and tests.\n\n\n### A.5 Domain\n\nA `domain` is a business subject area inside a `Root Block`.\n\nIt groups the logic that owns the same business object, capability, or invariant.\n\n```text\nbusiness/\n  auth/\n  billing/\n  podcast/\n  subscription/\n  account/\n```\n\nA `domain` is not a screen and not a route.\n\n- `route/auth.route.ext` receives auth-related input.\n- `ui/component/login/` renders a login screen.\n- `business/auth/` owns auth behavior: login, logout, register, recover password, permissions.\n\nInside a `domain`, use the Skill behavior nouns:\n\n```text\nbusiness/\n  auth/\n    action/\n    controller/\n    helper/\n    effect/\n```\n\nShort definition:\n\n> A `domain` is the business ownership boundary for related `actions`, `controllers`, `helpers`, and `effects` inside a `Root Block`.\n\n###### Domain and Data Model\n\nA `domain` can match a `Data Model` entity, but it does not have to.\n\n- A `Data Model` is durable and contractual data: tables, records, fields, relationships, schemas.\n- A `domain` is business ownership: the area that owns behavior, invariants, controllers, helpers, and effects.\n\nThey often overlap:\n\n```text\nData Model: User\nDomain: auth or account\n\nData Model: Subscription\nDomain: subscription or billing\n\nData Model: Podcast\nDomain: podcast\n```\n\nThey can also diverge:\n\n```text\nDomain: checkout\nData Models: cart, user, subscription, payment, invoice\n\nDomain: auth\nData Models: user, session, permission, token\n\nDomain: search\nData Models: podcast, tag, author\n```\n\nRule:\n\n> A `domain` is derived from business behavior and invariants, not mechanically from table names or model names.\n\nIf one `Data Model` owns a coherent lifecycle, it may become one `domain`. If a lifecycle crosses several `Data Models`, the `domain` should follow the lifecycle, not the storage shape.\n\n\n\n### A.6 Screen || Page\n\nA `screen` or `page` is a user-facing UI surface inside a frontend, client, or mobile `Root Block`.\n\nIt is the presentation composition that the operator can see or interact with.\n\nA `screen` or `page` can:\n\n- render `components`\n- read `Runtime State`\n- emit `inputs`\n- display `effects` feedback\n\nA `screen` or `page` is not a `domain`.\n\nA `screen` or `page` can involve several `domains` at the same time.\n\nExample:\n\n```text\nui/\n   component/\n      login/\n      checkout/\n      account-settings/\n   style/\n      login/\n      checkout/\n      account-settings/\n```\n\n*checkout* as a screen may involve:\n\n```text\nbusiness/\n  cart/\n  account/\n  subscription/\n  payment/\n```\n\nA `screen` or `page` is also not a *route*.\n\n- A *route* receives navigation or browser input.\n- A `screen` or `page` renders the UI surface.\n- A `controller` owns behavior after an `action` is created.\n- A `domain` owns business logic and invariants.\n\nRule:\n\n> A `screen` or `page` is a UI composition boundary, not a business ownership boundary.\n\n### A.7 Component\n\nA `component` is a UI building block.  \n\nIt renders part of a `screen` or `page`.  \n\nA `component` can receive data, display state, and emit user inputs like clicks, typing, or gestures.  \n\nA `component` does not own business logic. Business logic belongs to `controllers` inside `business/{domain}`.  \n\n\n\n\n### A.8 Test\nProves the full flow through `input`, `action`, `controller`, `helper`, and `effect` with the `help` of `telemetry`\n\n### A.9 Input\nA named entry condition *from outside* the behavior. It is part of the `spec` surface, not an execution unit.  \n> Examples: browser load, click, pointer drag, HTTP request, file watcher event, server refresh event.\n\n### A.10 Action\nCommand **payload** describing what happened or what is requested.\n\n### A.11 Controller\nBehavior owner. It branches, orchestrates, and decides the path.  \nIt **DOES NOT** contains implementation details, only branching, functions calls: `helpers`, `effects` and `telemetry`\n\n### A.12 Helper\n*Implementation extraction* from `controller` logic.  \nIt may be sync or async and may do IO.\n\n> Exemple: parsing text, validating data, querying a database, writing a file, deriving a branch decision, formatting output, calculating geometry, normalizing values or loading configuration.\n\n### A.13 Effect\nFinal output call; called by the `controller` with no expected response.  \nA `controller` can call several `effects` along the execution. \n\n> Exemple: Effects are final output calls used by controllers for things like publishing a state change, emitting a UI update, sending a response, notifying another system, committing a visible write result, or reporting telemetry.\n\n### A.14 Telemetry\n\n`Telemetry` is the execution evidence emitted during the flow so `tests`, `operators`, and `stack trace` can prove what happened.\n\nIt records things like the selected `controller branch`, `helper` calls, `effect` calls, `arguments`, `timing`, `errors`.  \n\n`Telemetry` is *observational*: it may report execution, but it **MUST NOT** decide behavior, replace controller branching, or become the source of truth for the result.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f4568-3024-76b3-82dd-294e499393b6"}}}

+    skipCardIds: new Set(Object.keys(mutation.geometry?.cards ?? {})),
+    skipAnnotationIds: new Set([
+      ...Object.keys(mutation.geometry?.zones ?? {}),
+      ...Object.keys(mutation.geometry?.groups ?? {})
+    ])
+  };

::html[Goal Linked Specs Summary](.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/assets/goal-linked-specs-summary/summary.html)

## A. Source Boundary

1. **Allowed source set.** This card uses the `Decision OS Context`, `PO Goal Analysis Format`, and `Goal Object UX` cards, the operator thread on this card, source files, tests, and `README.md`. It does not use `.decision-os/specs.json` or any spec-ledger card body as a source for linked specs.
2. **Spec-id rule.** A `spec id` is preserved only when the id appears in code or test evidence, for example `frontend/index.html` `data-spec` attributes or executable test headers. If the codebase shows behavior but no durable id, the `spec id` is recorded as `unknown`.
3. **Base goal.** Create an interface inside Decision OS that lets a human operator read and inspect PO goal-analysis report results for the current goal. The current goal is recursive: build the process and interface for seeing how a goal fits into the existing product.
4. **Context report fact.** Decision OS is a local browser canvas, TypeScript backend ledger server, and workspace-local `.decision-os` state. The current Next Features surface is `tasks-system`, shown as `Tasks System` in `.decision-os/state.json` and as `Ledger: Next Features` in `.decision-os/ledgers-canvas.json`.
5. **Goal-object fact.** The existing `Goal Object UX` card defines `Goal`, `Reports`, `Specs`, and `Tasks` as separate objects, and its global goal cockpit direction exposes `Specs`, `Reports`, and `Tasks` as tabs.

---

## B. Goal Spec Link

1. **Goal need.** The operator needs a readable goal-analysis interface that shows how the active goal relates to product context, technical context, UX context, linked specs, missing specs, and gaps.
2. **Affected product area.** The affected surface is the Decision OS ledger canvas, especially the `tasks-system` Next Features ledger, card Markdown rendering, thread inspector, report-card assets, and potential goal-cockpit navigation.
3. **Affected workflow.** The workflow is: operator creates or states a goal, agent/context report extracts facts, Decision OS presents linked specs and reports, operator inspects rows or opens threads, and later work can derive tasks or report ledgers from that factual state.
4. **Affected actor or role.** The primary actor is the **operator**. Supporting roles are the **agent** that extracts and writes durable state, the **frontend runtime** that renders the interface, and the **backend server** that hydrates and persists ledger files.
5. **Relevant context fact.** The context card states that report UX boundaries are unresolved: reports could be a card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, or embedded reader. The codebase already supports route-addressed ledgers, Markdown cards, image carousels, HTML embeds, threads, and voice notes.
6. **Current behavior.** Report facts can be stored in card Markdown, report mockups can be shown through adjacent images or active-ledger HTML embeds, threads attach operator feedback to cards, and ledgers load through `/decision-os/state` and `/decision-os/<tab>`.
7. **Expected behavior.** The goal-linked spec surface should show the base goal, goal/spec link fields, linked specs with source and relevance, missing specs, and gaps. It should remain facts-only: no recommendation, selected path, approval gate, or implementation plan.
8. **Acceptance signal.** The `Goal Linked Specs` card contains source-traceable entries for `goal need`, `affected product area`, `affected workflow`, `actor`, `context fact`, `current behavior`, `expected behavior`, `acceptance signal`, linked specs, missing specs, and spec gaps, with no direct spec-ledger extraction.

---

## C. Linked Specs

1. **`e6a91d34` - decision-os state drives ledger tabs and routes.** **Source:** `frontend/index.html`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-decision-os-state.ts`, and `tests/browser/navigation/decision-os-state-drives-ledger-tabs-and-routes.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** a goal-analysis interface must be reachable from the active ledger registry, and `tasks-system` is the current Next Features ledger.
2. **`f2d6c8b1` - Tab click loads the active ledger graph into the canvas.** **Source:** `frontend/index.html`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-active-ledger-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/render-ledger-surface.ts`, and `tests/browser/navigation/tab-click-loads-the-active-ledger-graph-into-the-canvas.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** report, spec, and task surfaces must render as active ledger graph state, not detached static pages.
3. **`cd58fd49` - card descriptions are parsed and rendered as markdown.** **Source:** `tests/browser/card/card-descriptions-are-parsed-and-rendered-as-markdown.spec.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/parse-ledger-card-markdown.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/component/render-ledger-card-markdown.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** the current report and spec-link inventory can live in a durable Markdown card without a schema change.
4. **`unknown` - Markdown tables, images, and HTML embeds are shared card/thread render blocks.** **Source:** `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/parse-ledger-card-markdown.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/component/render-ledger-card-media.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/component/render-ledger-card-html-embeds.ts`, `frontend/test/runtime/card-markdown-images.integration.test.ts`, and `frontend/test/runtime/card-markdown-html-embeds.integration.test.ts`. **Relation:** `support` and `constrain`. **Goal relevance:** readable report output can use tables, screenshots, and embedded HTML, but embeds must satisfy active-ledger asset rules.
5. **`eaced0c9`, `667ae9a9`, `5f8c7152`, `cc7ed3b4`, `f72a6d31` - thread model, conversation aggregation, preserved history, card-targeted notes, and active target title.** **Source:** `frontend/index.html`, `frontend/src/runtime/thread/effect/render-thread-panel.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/thread/effect/render-thread-notes.ts`, and `tests/browser/thread/*.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** linked specs and report rows can hand operator feedback to existing thread history, but the current confirmed target is still card or zone level.
6. **`d38927c1`, `747b461e`, `8b1ff788`, `6cc37b58`, `b5a783cd`, `c6f91a24`, `c0c42d20` - voice recording, thread scoping, upload, transcription status, shortcuts, and optional transcription.** **Source:** `frontend/index.html`, `frontend/src/runtime/input/controller/handle-keyboard.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/voice/*`, and `tests/browser/voice/*.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `adjacent` and `constrain`. **Goal relevance:** the goal-object UX mentions rephrasing a spec by voice; code supports thread voice capture, but does not yet show a goal-spec-row attachment model.
7. **`70000001-70000007` - server routes serve ledgers, accept edits, persist JSON, create ledgers, and index `.decision-os` tabs.** **Source:** `backend/test/routing/server-ledger-routing.integration.test.ts` and `backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts`. **Relation:** `support` and `constrain`. **Goal relevance:** report ledgers or goal ledgers must pass through the authoritative backend route and persistence model.
8. **`9c31f0a4` - Ledgers in `.decision-os` load as default tabs unless invalid.** **Source:** `backend/test/ledger/decision-os-default-tabs.integration.test.ts` and `backend/src/business/ledger/controller/load-tab-ledgers-controller.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** if a report result is represented as a real ledger, it needs a valid state registry entry.
9. **`9d1b7c36` - refresh preserves canvas continuity during operator work.** **Source:** `tests/browser/refresh/the-refresh-system-preserves-canvas-continuity-during-operator-work.spec.ts`, `backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/*`. **Relation:** `constrain`. **Goal relevance:** agent edits to report/spec-link cards should not disrupt the operator's current canvas or thread context.
10. **`c4e8b91a` - Cards indicate when the latest thread answer is from the agent.** **Source:** `tests/browser/card/cards-indicate-when-the-latest-thread-answer-is-from-the-agent.spec.ts` and `frontend/src/runtime/card/helper/card-has-agent-last-answer.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** treated goal-analysis notes need visible feedback that the latest unanswered operator request was answered.
11. **`c5a84d77` - Specs and data ledgers are available from decision-os `.decision-os`.** **Source:** `tests/browser/refresh/specs-and-data-ledgers-are-available-from-decision-os.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `non-goal` for this card. **Goal relevance:** the product can serve the spec ledger, but the operator explicitly excluded any spec ledger as an extraction source for this research pass.

---

## D. Missing Specs

1. **Goal object data spec.** **Implied requirement:** a goal needs durable identity, current statement, linked surfaces, and generated objects. **Missing acceptance signal:** no code-defined `Goal` object type or route was found. **Missing data spec:** `shared/schemas/core-types.ts` has `Card`, `Thread`, and `CanvasLedger`, but no `Goal`.
2. **Goal/spec link schema.** **Implied requirement:** persist `goal need`, `affected product area`, `workflow`, `actor`, `context fact`, `current behavior`, `expected behavior`, and `acceptance signal`. **Missing technical spec:** no `SpecLink` schema, mutation action, or renderer was found in source.
3. **Spec row review UX.** **Implied requirement:** each goal-linked spec row can expose approve, rephrase, reject, and thread actions. **Missing UX spec:** the code supports generic threads and voice, but no spec-row component, row-level thread target, or row review state exists.
4. **Report container boundary.** **Implied requirement:** report results need a durable readable surface. **Missing product-boundary spec:** the source evidence does not settle whether reports are cards, ledgers, goal-cockpit tabs, embedded readers, or a combination.
5. **Report ledger navigation.** **Implied requirement:** report cards can open report ledgers and zooming out can return to the global goal view. **Missing technical spec:** current code has ledgers-canvas zoom behavior and route state, but no report-ledger return contract tied to a goal object.
6. **Task flow representation.** **Implied requirement:** tasks can be list-first, grouped into flows, and optionally opened as a graph. **Missing data spec:** no task-flow object, system-prompt link, or formatted-output object was found in the current shared schema.
7. **Source policy enforcement.** **Implied requirement:** some research passes must extract specs only from a context card and codebase, not from a spec ledger. **Missing operational spec:** no CLI or runtime source-filter contract was found for enforcing this policy.
8. **Measurement and validation.** **Implied requirement:** acceptance for "visualize correctly" needs evidence. **Missing acceptance signal:** no analytics, usability observation, screen-reader audit, or live browser verification is attached to this card.

---

## E. Spec Gaps

1. **Contradiction.** Durable card formatting prefers numbered lists, but `parse-ledger-card-markdown.ts` only parses unordered `-` or `*` list syntax as a list block. Numbered lines render as paragraphs in the current card Markdown renderer.
2. **Unknown.** The codebase does not show a first-class `Goal`, `Report`, `SpecLink`, or `TaskFlow` object in `shared/schemas/core-types.ts`; this may be intentionally pending because the object model is still being designed.
3. **Unverified fact.** The context card states workspace counts and active adoption evidence, but this card did not run a live browser session or analytics check. Treat those counts as context-card evidence, not external usage proof.
4. **Source gap.** `frontend/index.html` contains many `data-spec` ids without titles; executable tests provide titles for many but not all ids. Rows above use test titles where available and mark unsupported titles as `unknown`.
5. **Ownership gap.** The context card says product-boundary decisions for reports, work queues, watcher agents, and goal objects remain operator-owned unless a future card assigns explicit ownership.
6. **Product-boundary decision.** The report surface is still unresolved between card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, and embedded reader. The current code supports all adjacent primitives but does not choose one.
7. **Technical constraint.** HTML embeds must live under `.decision-os/cards/<active-ledger>/assets/` and end in `.html`; `render-ledger-card-html-embeds.ts` rejects other locations.
8. **UX constraint.** Card detail rendering is expensive and hydrated only for visible cards. A long goal-analysis report must remain usable when the canvas is in low-detail or overview mode.
9. **Data constraint.** Current thread target kinds are `card`, `zone`, `group`, and `canvas`; there is no confirmed section-level or spec-row-level thread target.
10. **Dependency constraint.** Voice rephrase behavior depends on browser capture and optional OpenAI transcription configuration; the context card marks transcription as workspace-local and optional.

---

/**
 * WHAT: Browser spec assertion harness for the frontend root block.
 * WHY: The browser spec files must prove that ledger-authored behavior has implementation evidence.
 */
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync, existsSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';

const specs = JSON.parse(readFileSync('documentation/specs.json', 'utf8'));
const specById = new Map((specs.cards ?? []).map((card) => [card.id, card]));
const html = readFileSync('frontend/index.html', 'utf8');
const css = readRuntimeSource('frontend/assets');
const runtime = readRuntimeSource('frontend/src/runtime');
const backendServer = readFileSync('backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts', 'utf8');
const packageJson = readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8');

export async function assertFrontendSpec(title, specId, domain) {
  const spec = specById.get(specId);
  assert.ok(spec, `missing spec card ${specId}`);
  const haystack = `${html}\n${css}\n${runtime}\n${backendServer}\n${packageJson}`.toLowerCase();
  assert.ok(haystack.includes(specId.toLowerCase()), `${specId} is not tagged in implementation evidence`);
  for (const token of expectedTokens(title, domain, specId)) {
    assert.ok(haystack.includes(token.toLowerCase()), `${specId} missing implementation token: ${token}`);
  }
}

export async function assertBackendSpec(title, specId, domain) {
  await assertFrontendSpec(title, specId, domain);
}

function expectedTokens(title, domain, specId) {
  const text = `${title} ${domain}`.toLowerCase();
  const tokens = ['telemetry'];
  if (domain === 'canvas') tokens.push('canvas', 'renderCanvasSurface');
  if (domain === 'zone') tokens.push('zone', 'data-zone-id');
  if (domain === 'card') tokens.push('card', 'data-card-id');
  if (domain === 'selection') tokens.push('selection', 'resolve-selection-target');
  if (domain === 'group') tokens.push('group', 'data-group-id');
  if (domain === 'relationship') tokens.push('relationship', 'svg');
  if (domain === 'thread') tokens.push('thread', 'thread-panel');
  if (domain === 'voice') tokens.push('voice', 'voice-status');
  if (domain === 'navigation') tokens.push('data-tab', 'route');
  if (domain === 'toolbox') tokens.push('data-tool', 'renderToolbox');
  if (domain === 'refresh') tokens.push('refresh', 'fetch');
  if (text.includes('wheel') || specId === '30000005' || specId === '30000006') tokens.push("addEventListener('wheel'", 'canvas-wheel', 'calculate-viewport-transform');
  if (text.includes('ctrl') || text.includes('keyboard') || text.includes('escape') || text.includes('delete')) tokens.push('keyboard-shortcut');
  if (text.includes('drag') || text.includes('moved') || text.includes('pan')) tokens.push('pointermove', 'calculate-drag-delta');
  if (text.includes('marquee') || text.includes('selection box')) tokens.push('marquee', 'calculate-marquee-selection');
  if (text.includes('persist')) tokens.push('localStorage', 'commit-ledger-edit');
  if (text.includes('honeycomb')) tokens.push('--honeycomb-a', 'conic-gradient');
  if (text.includes('tiling scale')) tokens.push('background-size', '--canvas-honeycomb-width');
  if (text.includes('glow')) tokens.push('--glow');
  if (text.includes('notes') || text.includes('conversation')) tokens.push('open-card-thread', 'open-zone-thread');
  if (text.includes('transcription')) tokens.push('request-transcription', 'transcriptionStatus');
  if (text.includes('server') || text.includes('api') || text.includes('fetch')) tokens.push('createServer', 'application/json');
  if (text.includes('typescript')) tokens.push('.ts');
  if (text.includes('no bundler')) tokens.push('type=\"module\"', '/src/runtime/canvas-runtime.ts');
  if (text.includes('playwright')) tokens.push('tests/browser');
  if (text.includes('stylesheet') || text.includes('css')) tokens.push('canvas.css');
  if (text.includes('arrow')) tokens.push('marker', 'path');
  if (text.includes('label')) tokens.push('text');
  if (text.includes('brightness')) tokens.push('--zone-label-min-brightness-mix', '--zone-label-color');
  return Array.from(new Set(tokens));
}

assert.ok(existsSync('frontend/src/runtime/canvas-runtime.ts'));

function readRuntimeSource(path) {
  return readdirSync(path).sort().map((entry) => {
    const fullPath = `${path}/${entry}`;
    return statSync(fullPath).isDirectory() ? readRuntimeSource(fullPath) : readFileSync(fullPath, 'utf8');
  }).join('\n');
}
````

````text
import { state } from '../../state.js';

export type CanvasRect = { left: number; top: number; right: number; bottom: number; width: number; height: number };
export type LedgerGeometry = { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };

type LedgerRecord = Record<string, unknown>;

function finiteNumber(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
  const number = Number(value);
  return Number.isFinite(number) ? number : fallback;
}

export function ledgerCardGeometry(card: LedgerRecord): LedgerGeometry {
  return {
    x: finiteNumber(card.x, 0),
    y: finiteNumber(card.y, 0),
    width: Math.max(220, finiteNumber(card.w ?? card.width, 280)),
    height: Math.max(132, finiteNumber(card.h ?? card.height, 132))
  };
}

export function ledgerAnnotationGeometry(annotation: LedgerRecord): LedgerGeometry {
  const minWidth = annotation.variant === 'group' ? 220 : 180;
  const minHeight = annotation.variant === 'group' ? 160 : 140;
  return {
    x: finiteNumber(annotation.x, 0),
    y: finiteNumber(annotation.y, 0),
    width: Math.max(minWidth, finiteNumber(annotation.width ?? annotation.w, 280)),
    height: Math.max(minHeight, finiteNumber(annotation.height ?? annotation.h, 180))
  };
}

export function geometryToRect(geometry: LedgerGeometry): CanvasRect {
  return {
    left: geometry.x,
    top: geometry.y,
    right: geometry.x + geometry.width,
    bottom: geometry.y + geometry.height,
    width: geometry.width,
    height: geometry.height
  };
}

export function activeLedgerCardRectMap(): Map<string, CanvasRect> {
  const ledger = state.activeLedger as { cards?: unknown } | null;
  const cards = Array.isArray(ledger?.cards) ? ledger.cards as LedgerRecord[] : [];
  const entries: Array<[string, CanvasRect]> = [];
  for (const card of cards) {
    const id = String(card.id ?? '');
    if (id) entries.push([id, geometryToRect(ledgerCardGeometry(card))]);
  }
  return new Map(entries);
}

export function activeLedgerCardMap(): Map<string, LedgerRecord> {
  const ledger = state.activeLedger as { cards?: unknown } | null;
  const cards = Array.isArray(ledger?.cards) ? ledger.cards as LedgerRecord[] : [];
  const entries: Array<[string, LedgerRecord]> = [];
  for (const card of cards) {
    const id = String(card.id ?? '');
    if (id) entries.push([id, card]);
  }
  return new Map(entries);
}

export function activeLedgerAnnotationMap(): Map<string, LedgerRecord> {
  const ledger = state.activeLedger as { annotations?: unknown } | null;
  const annotations = Array.isArray(ledger?.annotations) ? ledger.annotations as LedgerRecord[] : [];
  const entries: Array<[string, LedgerRecord]> = [];
  for (const annotation of annotations) {
    const id = String(annotation.id ?? '');
    if (id) entries.push([id, annotation]);
  }
  return new Map(entries);
}

export function patchLedgerCardGeometry(card: LedgerRecord, geometry: LedgerGeometry): LedgerGeometry {
  const current = ledgerCardGeometry(card);
  const next = {
    x: Number.isFinite(geometry.x) ? geometry.x : current.x,
    y: Number.isFinite(geometry.y) ? geometry.y : current.y,
    width: Number.isFinite(geometry.width) ? Math.max(220, geometry.width) : current.width,
    height: Number.isFinite(geometry.height) ? Math.max(132, geometry.height) : current.height
  };
  card.x = next.x;
  card.y = next.y;
  card.w = next.width;
  card.h = next.height;
  return next;
}

export function patchLedgerAnnotationGeometry(annotation: LedgerRecord, geometry: LedgerGeometry): LedgerGeometry {
  const current = ledgerAnnotationGeometry(annotation);
  const minWidth = annotation.variant === 'group' ? 220 : 180;
  const minHeight = annotation.variant === 'group' ? 160 : 140;
  const next = {
    x: Number.isFinite(geometry.x) ? geometry.x : current.x,
    y: Number.isFinite(geometry.y) ? geometry.y : current.y,
    width: Number.isFinite(geometry.width) ? Math.max(minWidth, geometry.width) : current.width,
    height: Number.isFinite(geometry.height) ? Math.max(minHeight, geometry.height) : current.height
  };
  annotation.x = next.x;
  annotation.y = next.y;
  annotation.width = next.width;
  annotation.height = next.height;
  return ledgerAnnotationGeometry(annotation);
}

export function selectedLedgerGeometryPayload(selection = state.selection): {
  cards: Record<string, LedgerGeometry>;
  zones: Record<string, LedgerGeometry>;
  groups: Record<string, LedgerGeometry>;
} {
  const cards = activeLedgerCardMap();
  const annotations = activeLedgerAnnotationMap();
  const payload = { cards: {}, zones: {}, groups: {} } as {
    cards: Record<string, LedgerGeometry>;
    zones: Record<string, LedgerGeometry>;
    groups: Record<string, LedgerGeometry>;
  };
  for (const id of selection.cardIds as string[]) {
    const card = cards.get(id);
    if (card) payload.cards[id] = ledgerCardGeometry(card);
  }
  for (const id of selection.zoneIds as string[]) {
    const annotation = annotations.get(id);
    if (annotation) payload.zones[id] = ledgerAnnotationGeometry(annotation);
  }
  for (const id of selection.groupIds as string[]) {
    const annotation = annotations.get(id);
    if (annotation) payload.groups[id] = ledgerAnnotationGeometry(annotation);
  }
  return payload;
}
````

import { renderRelationshipOverlay } from '../../relationship/effect/render-relationship-overlay.js';
import { renderCanvasControlOverlay } from '../../canvas/effect/render-canvas-control-overlay.js';
import { state } from '../../state.js';
import { telemetry } from '../../telemetry/effect/telemetry.js';
import { activeLedgerCardMap, ledgerCardGeometry, patchLedgerCardGeometry, type LedgerGeometry } from '../../ledger/helper/active-ledger-geometry.js';
import { renderGeometry } from '../../canvas/helper/render-density.js';

export function resizeSelectedCard(dx: number, dy: number): void {
  const card = state.pointer?.target as HTMLElement | null;
  if (!card) return;
  const current = state.activeLedger && card.dataset.cardId
    ? ledgerCardGeometry(activeLedgerCardMap().get(card.dataset.cardId) ?? {})
    : { x: card.offsetLeft, y: card.offsetTop, width: card.offsetWidth, height: card.offsetHeight };
  const handle = state.pointer.resizeHandle as HTMLElement | null;
  const west = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('nw') || handle?.classList.contains('sw'));
  const east = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('ne') || handle?.classList.contains('se'));
  const north = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('nw') || handle?.classList.contains('ne'));
  const south = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('sw') || handle?.classList.contains('se'));
  const minWidth = 220;
  const minHeight = 132;
  let nextLeft = current.x;
  let nextTop = current.y;
  let nextWidth = current.width;
  let nextHeight = current.height;
  if (west) {
    const clampedDx = Math.min(dx, current.width - minWidth);
    nextLeft = current.x + clampedDx;
    nextWidth = current.width - clampedDx;
  }
  if (east) nextWidth = Math.max(minWidth, current.width + dx);
  if (north) {
    const clampedDy = Math.min(dy, current.height - minHeight);
    nextTop = current.y + clampedDy;
    nextHeight = current.height - clampedDy;
  }
  if (south) nextHeight = Math.max(minHeight, current.height + dy);
  const geometry = { x: nextLeft, y: nextTop, width: nextWidth, height: nextHeight };
  if (state.activeLedger && card.dataset.cardId) {
    const ledgerCard = activeLedgerCardMap().get(card.dataset.cardId);
    if (ledgerCard) patchLedgerCardGeometry(ledgerCard, geometry);
  }
  patchCardBox(card, geometry);
  renderRelationshipOverlay();
  renderCanvasControlOverlay();
  telemetry('render-card-layer', { spec: '60000006', resized: card.dataset.cardId, geometry });
}

function patchCardBox(card: HTMLElement, geometry: LedgerGeometry): void {
  const renderedGeometry = state.activeLedger ? renderGeometry(geometry) : geometry;
  card.style.left = `${renderedGeometry.x}px`;
  card.style.top = `${renderedGeometry.y}px`;
  card.style.width = `${renderedGeometry.width}px`;
  card.style.height = `${renderedGeometry.height}px`;
  card.style.minHeight = `${renderedGeometry.height}px`;
  card.dataset.sizeCacheWidth = String(geometry.width);
  card.dataset.sizeCacheHeight = String(geometry.height);
  card.style.setProperty('--card-size-cache-width', `${geometry.width}px`);
  card.style.setProperty('--card-size-cache-height', `${geometry.height}px`);
}
````

import { state } from '../../state.js';
import { renderCanvasControlOverlay } from '../../canvas/effect/render-canvas-control-overlay.js';
import { renderZoneLabelOverlay } from './render-zone-label-overlay.js';
import { telemetry } from '../../telemetry/effect/telemetry.js';
import { activeLedgerAnnotationMap, ledgerAnnotationGeometry, patchLedgerAnnotationGeometry, type LedgerGeometry } from '../../ledger/helper/active-ledger-geometry.js';
import { renderGeometry } from '../../canvas/helper/render-density.js';

export function resizeSelectedZone(dx: number, dy: number): void {
  const zone = state.pointer?.target as HTMLElement | null;
  if (!zone) return;
  const id = zone.dataset.zoneId ?? zone.dataset.groupId ?? '';
  const ledgerAnnotation = state.activeLedger && id ? activeLedgerAnnotationMap().get(id) : undefined;
  const current = ledgerAnnotation
    ? ledgerAnnotationGeometry(ledgerAnnotation)
    : { x: zone.offsetLeft, y: zone.offsetTop, width: zone.offsetWidth, height: zone.offsetHeight };
  const handle = state.pointer.resizeHandle as HTMLElement | null;
  const west = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('nw') || handle?.classList.contains('sw'));
  const east = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('ne') || handle?.classList.contains('se'));
  const north = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('nw') || handle?.classList.contains('ne'));
  const south = Boolean(handle?.classList.contains('sw') || handle?.classList.contains('se'));
  const minWidth = zone.dataset.groupId ? 220 : 180;
  const minHeight = zone.dataset.groupId ? 160 : 140;
  let nextLeft = current.x;
  let nextTop = current.y;
  let nextWidth = current.width;
  let nextHeight = current.height;
  if (west) {
    const clampedDx = Math.min(dx, current.width - minWidth);
    nextLeft = current.x + clampedDx;
    nextWidth = current.width - clampedDx;
  }
  if (east) nextWidth = Math.max(minWidth, current.width + dx);
  if (north) {
    const clampedDy = Math.min(dy, current.height - minHeight);
    nextTop = current.y + clampedDy;
    nextHeight = current.height - clampedDy;
  }
  if (south) nextHeight = Math.max(minHeight, current.height + dy);
  const geometry = { x: nextLeft, y: nextTop, width: nextWidth, height: nextHeight };
  if (ledgerAnnotation) patchLedgerAnnotationGeometry(ledgerAnnotation, geometry);
  patchZoneBox(zone, geometry);
  renderZoneLabelOverlay();
  renderCanvasControlOverlay();
  telemetry(zone.dataset.groupId ? 'render-group-layer' : 'render-zone-layer', { resized: id, geometry });
}

function patchZoneBox(zone: HTMLElement, geometry: LedgerGeometry): void {
  const renderedGeometry = state.activeLedger ? renderGeometry(geometry) : geometry;
  zone.style.left = `${renderedGeometry.x}px`;
  zone.style.top = `${renderedGeometry.y}px`;
  zone.style.width = `${renderedGeometry.width}px`;
  zone.style.height = `${renderedGeometry.height}px`;
  zone.style.minHeight = `${renderedGeometry.height}px`;
}

/**
 * WHAT: Runtime tests for transform-only canvas pan performance.
 * WHY: Canvas pan should not pay scale/detail-mode or unsampled telemetry costs on every pointermove.
 */
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { derivePointerIntent, ctrlPanOnlySpec } from '../../src/runtime/gesture/helper/derive-pointer-intent.js';
import { state } from '../../src/runtime/state.js';

const root = new URL('../../../', import.meta.url);

function source(path: string): string {
  return readFileSync(new URL(path, root), 'utf8');
}

test('canvas pan uses a transform-only path with sampled performance telemetry', () => {
  const pointerMove = source('frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-move.ts');
  const panTransform = source('frontend/src/runtime/canvas/effect/apply-pan-viewport-transform.ts');
  const panTelemetry = source('frontend/src/runtime/gesture/effect/emit-pan-performance-telemetry.ts');
  const pointerDown = source('frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-down.ts');
  const panningEffects = source('frontend/src/runtime/gesture/effect/schedule-panning-effects.ts');
  const finishPointer = source('frontend/src/runtime/gesture/effect/finish-pointer.ts');
  const pointHelper = source('frontend/src/runtime/gesture/helper/point.ts');
  const canvasCss = source('frontend/assets/canvas/canvas-layer.css');
  assert.match(pointerMove, /applyPanViewportTransform/);
  assert.match(pointerMove, /emitPanPerformanceTelemetry/);
  assert.match(pointerMove, /if \(isPan\)[\s\S]*return;/);
  assert.match(pointerMove, /const canvasPointer = isPan \? state\.pointer\.currentCanvas : canvasPoint\(pointer\)/);
  assert.match(panTransform, /content\.style\.transform/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(panTransform, /updateDetailMode/);
  assert.match(panTelemetry, /pan-frame-performance/);
  assert.match(panTelemetry, /frame === 1 \|\| input\.durationMs >= 8 \|\| frame % 12 === 0/);
  assert.match(pointerDown, /startedAt: now/);
  assert.match(pointHelper, /cachedCanvasBounds/);
  assert.match(pointHelper, /invalidateCanvasPointBounds/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(pointerDown, /classList\.(?:add|toggle)\('is-panning'/);
  assert.match(pointerMove, /schedulePanningEffects\(\)/);
  assert.match(finishPointer, /clearPanningEffects\(\)/);

import { state } from '../../state.js';
import { sendActiveLedgerMutation } from '../../ledger/effect/send-active-ledger-mutation.js';
import { readPersistedState } from '../helper/read-persisted-state.js';

let viewportPersistenceTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;

export function scheduleViewportPersistence(delayMs = 140): void {
  state.viewports = { ...(state.viewports ?? {}), [state.activeTab]: { ...state.viewport } };
  if (state.activeTab === 'surface') state.surfaceViewport = { ...state.viewport };
  if (viewportPersistenceTimer) clearTimeout(viewportPersistenceTimer);
  viewportPersistenceTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    viewportPersistenceTimer = null;
    if (state.canvasMode === 'ledgers') {
      void sendActiveLedgerMutation({ action: 'patch-viewport', viewport: { ...state.viewport } });
    }
    const persisted = readPersistedState();
    localStorage.setItem('decision-os.canvas.state', JSON.stringify({
      ...persisted,
      viewport: state.viewport,
      viewports: state.viewports,
      activeTab: state.activeTab,
      railCollapsed: state.railCollapsed
    }));
  }, delayMs);
}
````

````text
/**
 * WHAT: Coalesces wheel viewport updates and owns the short zoom-detail settle state.
 * WHY: Wheel bursts should update transform once per frame, then reconcile detail mode after input settles.
 */
import { applyViewportSettledEffects, applyViewportTransform } from './apply-viewport-transform.js';
import { hideCanvasControlOverlay } from './render-canvas-control-overlay.js';
import { syncRenderDensity } from '../helper/render-density.js';
import { renderLedgerSurface } from '../../ledger/effect/render-ledger-surface.js';
import { renderRelationshipOverlay } from '../../relationship/effect/render-relationship-overlay.js';
import { renderSelectionState } from '../../selection/effect/render-selection-state.js';
import { renderZoneLabelOverlay } from '../../zone/effect/render-zone-label-overlay.js';
import { clearViewportCardDetails, syncViewportCardDetails } from './sync-viewport-card-details.js';
import { updateDetailMode } from './update-detail-mode.js';
import { resumeCanvasMediaOverlay, suspendCanvasMediaOverlay } from './render-canvas-media-overlay.js';

let frame = 0;
let settleTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | 0 = 0;
let frameSettled = true;
let frameAnimated = false;

function nextFrame(callback: () => void): void {
  if (typeof requestAnimationFrame === 'function') requestAnimationFrame(callback);
  else setTimeout(callback, 0);
}

function finishZoomSettle(): void {
  settleTimer = 0;
  applyViewportSettledEffects();
  resumeCanvasMediaOverlay();
}

export function scheduleViewportTransform(zooming = true): void {
  if (zooming) {
    suspendCanvasMediaOverlay();
    hideCanvasControlOverlay();
    if (settleTimer) clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    settleTimer = setTimeout(finishZoomSettle, 120);
  }
  frameSettled = frameSettled && !zooming;
  frameAnimated = frameAnimated || zooming;
  if (frame) return;
  nextFrame(() => {
    frame = 0;
    const densityChanged = syncRenderDensity();
    if (densityChanged) {
      clearViewportCardDetails();
      renderLedgerSurface();
      renderSelectionState();
      renderZoneLabelOverlay();
      renderRelationshipOverlay();
    }
    const detailModeChanged = updateDetailMode();
    if (densityChanged || detailModeChanged) syncViewportCardDetails();
    const settled = frameSettled;
    const animated = frameAnimated && !densityChanged;
    frameSettled = true;
    frameAnimated = false;
    applyViewportTransform(settled, animated);
  });
  frame = 1;
}
````
